method: Each negative runs twice: in the simulator (generated JavaScript, honest checks) and at the proof server with the JavaScript checks that would refuse it bypassed in a patched copy of the generated contract; every other assert still throws in that copy, so a case that names one assert isolates it. Every patched copy proves the honest call of its circuit through itself: the cases of the checked hints, the readable texts the isolating forgeries and the shared checks at every place a value enters (sections hints, texts, isolate, places) and most others prove it before their own attempt; elsewhere the negatives of one copy in a section share the first control proved through it, and each result names its control (control.with). A forged byte argument above 8 bits travels through a copy that lets it past the type check and encodes it as given; the circuit's range check refuses it. A case passes only when it is refused at the expected layer, every named assert fired in the copy, and the refusal is attributed to the circuit under test. Each section ran in its own run from a freshly started proof server; each section draws its own deterministic values, so a run of one section draws what the full suite draws.
